supersedesNoOwnership: cache-keys.ts (bifrostKey) remains the single key-builder library. This audit found a semantics conflict inside an existing namespace it already builds, not a reason to build a second key library.
context: Raised by external review 2026-09-04, same day as BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01 shipped. That gate's canonical invalidateBitfrostPacket() is not reversed by this finding -- it correctly deletes bifrost:sem:packet:{packetKey} for the reward-cache identity. This audit found that invalidation is INCOMPLETE, not wrong: a second, incompatible identity sharing the same key prefix is untouched by it.

identityA.value: PacketCacheEntry (packetKey, featureId, summary, conceptIds, communityId, rewardScore)
identityA.liveCallersFound: zero external callers of setPacketCache/getPacketCache in sveltekit-frontend/src as of BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01's audit -- not re-verified in this pass

identityB.suffix: query_hash (sha256 of a query string, unrelated to any single packet)
writers: scripts/atlas/warm-bitfrost-semantic-cache.mjs also writes `bifrost:sem:packet:${packetKey}` at line 349 -- this second script uses identity A's shape, not B's; the conflict is specifically between atlas-reward-cache.ts + warm-bitfrost-semantic-cache.mjs (packetKey) vs warm-bifrost-semantic-cache.mjs (query_hash), i.e. between the two similarly-named warm scripts, not just app-code vs script.
identityB.value: a JSON blob keyed by query_hash containing source_refs[]/feature_id/token_hints/answer_hint/state -- a query-level result cache, per query-router.ts's own comment: 'Checks warm-bifrost-semantic-cache keys written by npm run bifrost:semantic:warm'
confirmedBy: scripts/cache/warm-bifrost-semantic-cache.mjs:10,137 (doc comment + real setex call using c.query_hash)

confirmedConflict.consequence: invalidateBitfrostPacket(redis, {packetKey}) correctly deletes identity A's entry for that packetKey. It has no way to find or delete any identity B (query-hash-keyed) cache entries that reference that packet in their source_refs, because there is no packetKey -> queryHash inverse index. A packet mutation can therefore leave a stale query-level cache hit that still points to pre-mutation source_refs/feature_id, even after BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01's fix runs.
confirmedConflict.invalidationOwnerFixScope: Proven and scoped exactly to identity A (packet-keyed reward cache + packet summary + feature cache). Never claimed to cover identity B. Not reversed by this finding.

bifrost:sem:feature:{feature_id}.identity: feature_id, single consistent meaning across all callers found
readers: query-router.ts (not directly confirmed reading this key in this pass)

bifrost:sem:intent:{intent_hash}.identity: sha256 of normalized query text -> resolves to a query_hash (an indirection layer, not a packet or feature identity)
bifrost:sem:intent:{intent_hash}.note: Consistently query-hash-indirection on both sides checked.

bitfrost:summary:packet:v1:{packet_key}.writers: not located in sveltekit-frontend/src as of BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01 (flagged there too)
bitfrost:summary:packet:v1:{packet_key}.note: The user-cited 'thousands of live bitfrost:summary:packet:v1 entries' claim was not independently re-verified with a live EXISTS/SCAN count in this pass -- treat as reported, not re-confirmed here.

bitfrost:retrieval:{queryHash} (legacy,.note: Legacy retrieval cache lane, distinct from the revision-qualified v2 lane below.

bitfrost:retrieval:v2:{sha256(canonical).identity: sha256 of a canonicalized request that presumably includes revision -- exact revision-qualification fields not verified line-by-line in this pass
bitfrost:retrieval:v2:{sha256(canonical).note: This is the 'revision-qualified retrieval cache' the reviewer correctly identified as architecturally preferable to an inverse-dependency-index approach for query-result invalidation. Worth building on for identity B's eventual fix, per the reviewer's own reasoning: a revision-qualified query cache key naturally becomes unreachable after a revision bump, without needing broad SCAN or an inverse index.

classificationOfInvalidateRedisCacheImpl.note: Re-scoped per this gate's request to classify beyond the 4 already found by BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01 (PRODUCTION_OWNER / PRODUCTION_DELEGATE / BOUNDED_SCRIPT / LEGACY_SCRIPT / DEAD / TEST / VALIDATION). Not exhaustively re-swept in this pass due to context budget -- the 4 already classified in BITFROST-INVALIDATION-OWNER-01's receipt stand (all now PRODUCTION_DELEGATE, delegating to the one PRODUCTION_OWNER, invalidateBitfrostPacket). A broader sweep for older/script-level invalidateRedisCache-shaped functions (summarizers, phase scripts, packet-truth scripts) was not performed this pass -- flagged as remaining Stage 1 work, not done.

recommendationForStage2: Do NOT rename bifrost:sem:packet:* yet, per explicit instruction. Two real options once ready: (a) migrate identity B (query-result cache) off the bifrost:sem:packet:* prefix entirely onto its own bifrost:sem:query:{query_hash} namespace (a prefix already reserved and unused per invalidate-atlas-cache-epoch.mjs's own pattern list, which already deletes bifrost:sem:query:* alongside bifrost:sem:packet:* -- suggesting bifrost:sem:query:* was the originally INTENDED name for identity B and warm-bifrost-semantic-cache.mjs simply wrote to the wrong prefix), or (b) make identity B revision-qualified like bitfrost:retrieval:v2 so stale entries become naturally unreachable. Recommend (a): it directly fixes the namespace collision at its root, and invalidate-atlas-cache-epoch.mjs's existing bifrost:sem:query:* pattern implies this was always the intended shape.
